mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior month signals monetary easing, reducing the cost of capital and increasing equity valuations, which produces positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1 percentage points over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 2.5%, it indicates restrictive monetary policy that increases the cost of capital, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 2.5.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and consumer spending (RSAFS) by more than 0.5% in the prior month signals robust economic growth that may trigger monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both increase > 0.5% in prior month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS and RSAFS both increase by more than 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.5%, it indicates a late-cycle expansion where the economy is near full employment, increasing recession risk and causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE < 3.5.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over the prior month signals manufacturing contraction, increasing recession risk and causing negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO declines by at least 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the prior month signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, producing positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of instances where HOUST increases by at least 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1150 thousand units, it indicates potential housing market overheating that may trigger monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances where HOUST > 1150.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 255), the Federal Reserve is likely to tighten monetary policy, increasing the cost of capital and causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 255.
